Replay

Dockyard service configuration

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
itch.io connections and local DNS

The selected Pi deployment serves wss://mc.laserturtle.net:62127/replay-room/dockyard, alongside the existing Scrapyard /rtc route and shared TURN relay. The files here also include generic templates for another deployment. Public-origin iframe checks and off-network acceptance are separate from local HTTPS/WSS and relay tests.

Serve the ordinary production export, including its PCK and Wasm files, from one HTTPS origin. Never publish the test-bridge project, browser profiles, enrollment databases, private fixture directories, certificates' private keys or TURN credentials. The Caddyfile sets the same COOP/COEP/CORP response headers used by the browser checks. It takes DOCKYARD_HTTPS_ADDRESS, DOCKYARD_WEB_ROOT, DOCKYARD_TLS_CERT and DOCKYARD_TLS_KEY from the operator's environment and uses supplied certificates. It performs no automatic certificate enrollment. Its syntax follows Caddy's header and TLS directives.

Use the existing Replay room service, built with the selected Native library and explicit static SQLite input. It owns enrollment, authority leases, signaling and relay credential issuance. It does not simulate Dockyard. Set REPLAY_ROOM_CHECKPOINT_MODEL=disabled; this release does not supply durable-world publication or host takeover. Use the selected artifact's exact DOCKYARD_LOBBY cohort in REPLAY_ROOM_CONTENT, with separate databases/services for incompatible cohorts. Native and Web cohorts differ.

Copy service.env.example to a private operator file, replace the paths/addresses and explicitly initialize the database once. Subsequent starts must not silently recreate a missing database. Run the service's prepared project with ODIN_SCRIPTS_DLL pointing to its exact scripts library. The service itself serves WSS using its certificate and key; the static-file Caddy server is separate.

For a public relay, complete turnserver.conf.template using the pinned Coturn configuration reference. The room service and Coturn share the server-only secret. Clients receive short lived credentials through authenticated membership. Set the listener/relay IPs, any actual NAT mapping and firewall rules for the chosen UDP/TCP/TLS listeners and relay port range. The public template deliberately has no loopback-peer exception; that exception belongs only to the isolated local tests.

Open the game with public routing configuration, for example:

Text
https://game.example.invalid/index.html?service=wss%3A%2F%2Frooms.example.invalid%3A49740&relay=1

The URL contains no credentials. Players choose a name and Host or Join; they share the explicit invitation code through Copy Invite. Invite codes are capabilities, so keep them out of logs, public URLs and screenshots. Recent Crew uses the stored membership, rather than reusing a consumed invitation. Serve the same qualified Wasm artifact to both browser players. Public Internet acceptance still requires two actual remote endpoints, valid public trust and recorded selected candidate pairs with transferred traffic. Local certificate pins and local TURN success do not establish that result.

itch.io connections and local DNS#

An itch page is a public origin. If the room hostname resolves to a private LAN address on the player's network, browser local-network restrictions can block the WebSocket before a room request reaches the proxy. The observed itch iframe does not delegate the local-network permission. A successful localhost preview or command-line WebSocket handshake does not test that permission boundary.

Compare the system resolver with a public resolver:

Shell
dig +short mc.laserturtle.net
dig @1.1.1.1 +short mc.laserturtle.net

For this public game endpoint, remove a local DNS rewrite to 10.0.0.10 so clients use the public DNS record. Keep LAN-only names separate. Restart the browser after the DNS correction. The existing public port and proxy paths remain the same. Keep the WSS hostname for certificate validation; changing the URL to an IP literal does not preserve that validation.

The retained itch-origin probes reproduced failures on both /rtc and /replay-room/dockyard with local DNS. Using public DNS restored WebSocket connections in Chrome and Firefox without disabling browser protections. Chrome reported ERR_BLOCKED_BY_LOCAL_NETWORK_ACCESS_CHECKS; Firefox reported a generic connection failure. The separate Firefox Source Map URL: null diagnostic concerns debugging metadata, not the WebSocket route. See Chrome's WebSocket rollout and the Local Network Access permission model.
